newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent falls sharply from high on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent falls sharply from high on profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures fell 60 cents from the day's high on Thursday afternoon as traders took profits from the week's $2.00 rally, brokers said.
The military confrontation between Iraq and the U.S. was still escalating, with eight U.S. stealth fighters set to leave for the Gulf on Thursday afternoon, U.S. defence officials said.
October Brent came off a post-Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel, falling to $23.71 per barrel by 1500 GMT, still 13 cents above Wednesday's close.
"We are seeing bouts of profit-taking, but no one is going short here," a broker said.
Prices peaked on market fears that Iraq might mount an assault against Kuwait after the latter agreed to serve as an base for an expected U.S. military strike on Iraq.
"People are talking things through. If there is an offensive by Iraq, it will be quickly quashed by the U.S. and oil supplies are not really threatened," one broker said.
"Also there is talk of producers pumping like crazy at these prices," he added.
However, he did not expect prices to fall much further, as NYMEX October crude futures were just above a support level at $24.50 per barrel.
IPE October gas oil also held onto some of the day's gains, standing $1.50 higher at $217.50 per tonne, having touched a high of $225.00.
The October gas oil/Brent crack spread was steady at $5.60 per barrel.
October became the prompt month this afternoon after September expired with 155,300 tonnes of outstanding positions at the close.
